heading.title: Locational Astrology: Maps, Relocation Charts, and Methods

generatorNote: This generator draws an astrocartography world map from your birth date, time, and birthplace. It is not a Local Space chart and not a single-city relocation chart.

intentAnchor.text: Locational astrology is the wider field for reading a birth chart against places on Earth. Astrocartography is one method inside that field. A relocation chart is another. This guide shows which question each method answers, then sends you to the free map or the one-city relocation chart on Astrocarto.org.

introduce.name: introduce
introduce.title: What the umbrella term actually covers
introduce.label: Definition
introduce.description: Locational astrology is any approach that connects a horoscope with a place on Earth. Astrocartography is the best-known technique inside it: Jim Lewis popularized maps that mark where planets were angular at a timed birth. A relocation chart is a different calculation for one city. Astrogeography is a looser label. Some writers use it for this whole field. Others use it for traditions that assign signs or planets to regions without projecting one person's birth chart. Check the output, not the nickname.

image.alt: Astrocarto.org map used as a starting point for place-based chart methods

items.title: Not a synonym for the map alone
items.description: Calling every location technique astrocartography hides the job each tool does. A world map answers where angular lines fall. A relocation chart answers how houses and angles reorder in one city. If a page promises a directional Local Space chart, that is a third job. This site's calculators cover the map and the one-city wheel.

image.alt: Planetary lines on a personal astrocartography map

items.title: Why birth time sits in the middle of the method
items.description: Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli move quickly. An approximate birth time can still support a broad look at the map, but it makes precise city conclusions less reliable. The same limit applies when a relocation chart rebuilds houses from a new Ascendant. If you only know the date, treat angle and house statements as exploratory.

image.alt: Chart angles that depend on birth time and place

items.title: A symbolic layer, not a relocation verdict
items.description: These methods do not prove that a place will cause love, money, a visa, or failure. They offer a symbolic frame for comparing themes. No planetary line is universally lucky, and a city with no nearby line is not automatically empty of meaning. Work, housing, cost, safety, healthcare, and legal status still decide whether a move is realistic.

feature.name: example
feature.title: A practical sequence for three candidate cities
feature.label: Example
feature.description: Suppose you are comparing Lisbon, Berlin, and Montreal. This sequence does not declare a winner. It shrinks an open question into evidence you can set beside real-world constraints.

items.title: Generate the map first
items.description: Enter your birth date, time, and birthplace in the generator on this page. Inspect which planet-and-angle combinations fall near each city. You are looking for different emphases, not a ranked list of best homes.

items.title: Keep one city for a closer read
items.description: If Berlin stays on the shortlist, note its distance from the lines you care about, then open the relocation chart for Berlin only. The map shows the wider pattern. The relocated wheel shows angles and houses for that one place.

items.title: Hand the shortlist to the where-to-live guide
items.description: When the original question is where you might live, continue with the where-to-live workflow. Match line themes to a goal, then check visas, work, and housing. The methods page stops at choosing the right calculation.

items.title: Read a line only after you know the angle
items.description: A Venus line on the Descendant is not the same topic as a Venus line on the Imum Coeli. If you need planet-and-angle meanings, use the lines hub and the map interpretation guide after the calculation, not instead of it.

faq.name: faq
faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Common questions about these methods
faq.description: Short answers for the questions that usually sit behind this search.

items.title: Is locational astrology the same as astrocartography?
items.description: Not exactly. Locational astrology is the broader field. Astrocartography is the world-map technique that marks where planets were angular at birth. A relocation chart and Local Space are other ways to connect a chart with place.

items.title: What is astrogeography?
items.description: Astrogeography is not one standard calculation. Some people use the word for this whole field. Others use it for systems that associate signs or planets with regions. Read the method and the output before you treat two maps as the same thing.

items.title: Does Astrocarto.org calculate Local Space?
items.description: No. Local Space looks at planetary directions from a chosen place on the local horizon. Astrocarto.org calculates an astrocartography map and a one-city relocation chart. This page explains the difference so the missing method is explicit.

items.title: Should I start with a world map or a relocation chart?
items.description: Start with the world map when the question is still open. Use the relocation chart when one city is already a serious candidate. Many people do both: scan first, then recalculate houses for a finalist.

items.title: What is an astro location chart?
items.description: The phrase can mean a planetary-line world map or a chart relocated to one city. A world map shows lines across Earth. A relocated chart recalculates angles and houses for one place. Check the output before comparing two results.

items.title: Can I create this map free?
items.description: Yes. The generator on this page creates the core astrocartography map from birth date, time, and birthplace. Guest sessions have a daily limit, and signing in allows more map sessions. Optional AI chat and city reports use credits shown before you spend them.

items.title: Which method should I use if I am deciding where to move?
items.description: Start with the world map to scan regions and cities. Use the relocation chart when one city is a serious candidate. Neither result chooses a home for you. Compare it with work, housing, visas, and cost, then continue with the where-to-live guide.

items.title: Can locational astrology name the best place to live?
items.description: No. It can show which themes a map or a relocated chart emphasizes. It cannot promise love, money, a visa, or a successful move. Pair the symbolic result with practical research, then use the where-to-live guide if housing is the decision.
